title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from p.34). A 'figure' F is a set S with a surjection f: S → I onto a finite (or arbitrary) ordered set of indices. This is essentially an Alexandrov ('ultra-') topology or poset-stratification. J ⊂ I is a closed part, i.e. a down-set; downward closure is needed for the construction below. G is the restriction of F to T = f^{-1}(J), indexed by J. A refinement G' ≤ G is a factorisation T → J' → J, with T → J' surjective and h_J: J' → J a 'coinitial surjection' of ordered sets.

Problem. Given G', extend it to a refinement F' ≤ F, S → I' → I, inducing G' on T. Equivalently, find a commutative square i': J' ↪ I', h: I' → I over i: J ↪ I with J' = h^{-1}(J).

Construction on p.35. Let K = J' ⊔ (I∖J) as a set. Give it the order that restricts to the given orders on J' and on I∖J. For α ∈ J' and β ∈ I∖J, set α ≤ β iff h_J(α) ≤ β in I. There are no relations β ≤ α, since J is a down-set.
- Transitivity holds because h_J is monotone; antisymmetry is immediate. J' is then a down-set (closed) in K.
- Define h_K: K → I as h_J on J' and the identity on I∖J. It is monotone and surjective.
- The square J' ↪ K → I, J' → J ↪ I commutes and is cartesian: J' = h_K^{-1}(J), and h_K induces an order isomorphism K∖J' ≅ I∖J.

Continuation on p.36. K is the final object among all such squares J' ↪ I' → I satisfying the cartesian condition. Given (I', h, i'), the comparison map I' → K is the identity on J' and h on I'∖J'.
- It is monotone. If x ∈ J' and y ∉ J', then h(x) ≤ h(y) gives x ≤ h(y) in K. The case x ∉ J', y ∈ J' cannot occur: J is a down-set, so h(x) ≤ h(y) ∈ J forces h(x) ∈ J, i.e. x ∈ J'.
- It is unique because h_K is the identity on the open complement.

Modern reading. K is the collage (cograph) of the order-profunctor (α, β) ↦ [h_J(α) ≤ β]. It is the poset analogue of Artin gluing along a closed/open decomposition: replace the closed stratum J by J' and keep the open part. K is the coarsest refinement of the index poset extending a refinement given on a closed part. It serves the 'algebra of figures': refinements of stratified figures can be extended from closed pieces. The following page then switches to the language of ultra-topologies (Alexandrov topologies) on parts of a space.
errors: The construction implicitly requires 'fermée' to mean down-closed (closed in the Alexandrov topology where closures are down-sets). Otherwise the order on K would need relations β ≤ α, and J' = h_K^{-1}(J) would not ensure that J' is closed in K. This is not stated on this page but is consistent with p.34.

The page does not check whether h_K is again a 'coinitial surjection' (the condition demanded of h in a refinement). It holds if h_J is one, since h_K is the identity off J', but this is left implicit.
Minor slip in the case list: '(α,β) ∈ J'' should read α, β ∈ J' (likewise for I∖J).

ideas.what: Gluing an ordered set J' (mapping to a closed part J ⊂ I) with the open complement I∖J, using the order α ≤ β iff h_J(α) ≤ β.
ideas.modern_name: Collage/cograph of a profunctor between posets; poset version of Artin gluing (recollement) along a closed–open decomposition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin gluing (Artin–Grothendieck–Verdier, SGA4); collages of profunctors in categorical folklore (Street and others)
ideas.where_published: Recollement of topoi along open/closed pieces appears in SGA4 IV (gluing); this exact poset construction is not known to me in published texts

ideas.what: Universal (final) property of K among cartesian squares J' → I' → I extending a refinement over a closed part.
ideas.modern_name: Terminal extension of a refinement of a poset-stratification from a closed union of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in stratified-space theory (no specific attribution)

ideas.what: Figures as subsets with Alexandrov ('ultra-') topologies or poset-indexed stratifications, refined by surjective/coinitial maps of index posets.
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified spaces (cf. Lurie, Higher Algebra, Appendix A; exit-path categories)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and stratified structures in general terms

missed.claim: Within an unpublished 'algebra of figures' (1986), Grothendieck sets up refinement of poset-stratified figures and proves a terminal-extension property. A refinement given on a closed part extends canonically, and coarsest-possibly, via the collage poset K = J' ⊔ I∖J. The mathematics is elementary, but it documents his formalism for tame/stratified 'figures'.
missed.quote: K = J' ⊔ I∖J ... α ≤ β ssi h_J(α) ≤ β dans I
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It shows him developing a combinatorial (finite-poset, Alexandrov-topology) foundation for tame topology in 1986, close to today's poset-stratified-space formalism. The construction itself is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but elementary order-theoretic gluing with a straightforward universal property. Its interest lies only in the context of the unpublished 'algèbre des figures' programme.
transcription_corrections: '(α,β)∈J'' and '(α,β)∈I∖J' should read 'α,β ∈ J'' and 'α,β ∈ I∖J'.
'V̄(J' = h_K^{-1}(J)' is likely 'i.e. J' = h_K^{-1}(J)' (the cartesian condition), followed by a remark that this condition determines things 'relativement'.
The margin note reads roughly 'explicitation des propriétés à poser/prouver', annotating the three-case description of the order.
'un diagramme commutatif d'ens. ordonnés' — the image shows J' ↪ K (labelled i), vertical maps h_J and h_K, and the bottom row J ↪ I (labelled i).
